title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Guiding Opinion on Pairing-up Support for the Work of Courts in Tibet
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Guiding Opinions on the Paired Assistance Work for the Courts in Tibet

Fa Fa [2010] No. 26

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Guiding Opinions on the Paired Assistance Work for the Courts in Tibet are hereby issued to you for earnest implementation.

July 9, 2010

Guiding Opinions on the Paired Assistance Work for the Courts in Tibet

In order to thoroughly implement the spirit of the Fifth Central Symposium on Work in Tibet, promote leapfrog development and long-term stability in Tibet's economy and society, and further enhance the ability of the courts in Tibet to serve the overall situation, administer justice for the people, promote development, and maintain stability, the following guiding opinions are hereby put forward regarding further efforts in the paired assistance work for the courts in Tibet:

I. Deeply understand the great significance of the assistance work for Tibet, and effectively strengthen the sense of responsibility, mission, and urgency.

1. Deepening the assistance work for Tibet is of great significance for vigorously promoting Tibet's economic development and social progress, maintaining ethnic unity, maintaining social stability, maintaining national security, building a national ecological security barrier, resisting international hostile forces' strategy of Westernization and division, creating a favorable international environment, and promoting Tibet's leapfrog development and long-term stability. Assisting Tibet is an important strategic decision of the Party Central Committee and an important part of the work of the people's courts. People's courts at all levels nationwide should, from the strategic height of the overall work of the Party and the state, further enhance their understanding of the importance and urgency of continuing to do a good job in the assistance work for Tibet.

II. Guiding Ideology and Basic Principles

2. Guiding ideology: Hold high the great banner of socialism with Chinese characteristics, take Deng Xiaoping Theory and the important thought of the "Three Represents" as guidance, thoroughly implement the Scientific Outlook on Development, adhere to the "Three Supremacies" work guiding ideology, adhere to the work theme of "serving the overall situation and administering justice for the people", closely focus on the three key tasks of deepening the resolution of social conflicts, social management innovation, and impartial and clean law enforcement, take intellectual assistance as the lead, take project assistance as the support, strive to further improve the overall quality of the court team in Tibet, further enhance judicial capacity, further improve infrastructure and equipment, and provide better judicial guarantees for building a new socialist Tibet that is united, democratic, prosperous, civilized, and harmonious.

3. The assistance work for Tibet shall adhere to the following principles: First, the principle of paired assistance. Maintain consistency with the paired assistance relations for Tibet determined by the Central Committee, and determine the paired assistance relations of the people's courts. Second, the principle of ensuring priorities. Under the premise of overall balance, focus on tilting towards the grassroots, the front line, and the people's livelihood. Third, the principle of rational planning. Combine long-term planning with phased arrangements, and combine solving current difficulties with long-term development.

III. Strengthen the Work on Talent and Intellectual Assistance for Tibet

4. Strive to solve the problem of the shortage of judges in the courts of Tibet. On the basis of reasonably distributing the increased staffing during the Eleventh Five-Year Plan period, the Supreme People's Court will actively coordinate with relevant central departments to appropriately increase the staffing of courts in Tibet. Carry out pilot reform work on the targeted recruitment and training system for political and legal cadres, and cultivate legal and bilingual talents of different academic levels for the courts in Tibet. Continue to carry out pilot work on the judicial examination in western ethnic minority regions. Earnestly promote the pilot work of judge assistants and the volunteer service action for grassroots people's courts in western regions, to alleviate the pressure of personnel shortage. Strengthen the occupational protection of judges, gradually improve the treatment of judges, and reduce the phenomenon of judge turnover.

5. Strive to do a good job in talent assistance for Tibet. Improve the selection and management of cadres sent to assist Tibet, perfect management methods and assessment mechanisms, strictly set selection conditions, improve the quality of selection, care about the work and life of cadres sent to assist Tibet, help solve their families' special difficulties, remove their worries, and enable them to work at ease in Tibet. On the basis of effectively completing the tasks of cadres sent to assist Tibet determined by the Central Committee, courts providing assistance that have the conditions may select outstanding judges to work in Tibet, and gradually expand the scope of work of cadres sent to assist Tibet to grassroots people's courts. According to the needs of the recipient courts, select network technical personnel to work in Tibet on a short-term basis, train network technical personnel, participate in the project review, quality supervision, project acceptance, and operation and maintenance of the network construction of the courts in Tibet, and solve problems in network operation. Actively coordinate with relevant departments such as organization and personnel to earnestly implement various policy treatments for cadres sent to assist Tibet.

6. Strengthen education and training work for the courts in Tibet. Formulate a work plan for education and training for the courts in Tibet, increase the support for education and training for the courts in Tibet, implement a free system for judges from Tibet to participate in mandatory training at the National Judges College, and gradually expand the scale of training. Regularly dispatch lecturer teams to Tibet for itinerant lectures, hold training classes for judges of the courts in Tibet at appropriate times, and dispatch experts to explain difficult and hot issues in judicial work. Contact experts and professors to provide pre-exam training for the judicial examination in Tibet, to improve the pass rate of the judicial examination in the courts in Tibet. Make full use of advanced technologies such as the internet, and actively promote distance education models.

7. Support the construction of legal book libraries in the courts of Tibet. Actively carry out the compilation and publication of training materials for judges in Tibetan and Chinese bilingualism. Continue to do a good job in presenting judicial newspapers and periodicals such as the People's Court Daily and the Supreme People's Court Gazette, as well as relevant legal books, to the courts in Tibet. Courts providing paired assistance shall, based on actual circumstances, present relevant legal books and other learning and reference materials.

IV. Strengthen Business Guidance for the Courts in Tibet

8. Strengthen guidance on case adjudication. In particular, strengthen guidance on the adjudication of cases endangering national security, cases involving the Qinghai-Tibet Railway, group cases arising from disputes over resources such as mines, grasslands, and Cordyceps sinensis, and cases seriously endangering social security. For major and sensitive cases concerning social stability and national welfare and people's livelihood, the Supreme People's Court shall strengthen supervision and guidance, actively communicate with the Party Committee and Government of the Tibet Autonomous Region, and improve the targetedness and effectiveness of the work.

9. Actively carry out research work. Increase support for the research work of the courts in Tibet, and give preference in key research project bidding, etc. Conduct in-depth research on cases involving the Qinghai-Tibet Railway, tourism cases, group cases arising from disputes over resources such as mines, grasslands, and Cordyceps sinensis, and promptly put forward guiding opinions.

10. Increase the intensity of work exchanges. Courts providing assistance shall proactively introduce their advanced experience and successful practices in adjudication work, judicial reform, court management, etc. to the courts in Tibet. Each year, the courts in Tibet may select some judges or staff members to take temporary posts or follow cases for study in courts in the interior. Through two-way exchanges and study, continuously improve the case handling quality, case handling efficiency, and judicial management level of the courts in Tibet.

V. Strengthen Material Assistance Work for Tibet

11. Promote the establishment of a normal growth mechanism for case handling and public expenses of the courts in Tibet. In view of the heavy task of maintaining stability in the courts of Tibet, the high social control and case handling costs of the court system, and the actual situation of increasing cases, in accordance with the spirit of the "Notice of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China on Forwarding the 'Opinions of the Central Political and Legal Committee on Several Issues concerning Deepening the Reform of the Judicial System and Working Mechanism'", the Supreme People's Court will actively coordinate with the Ministry of Finance to promote the establishment of a normal growth mechanism for case handling business and public expenses of the courts in Tibet, ensuring that the case handling business expenses required by the courts in Tibet are fully borne by the central finance.

12. Increase investment in the business equipment construction of the courts in Tibet. When jointly formulating equipment allocation standards for people's courts with the Ministry of Finance, the Supreme People's Court shall fully consider the current situation of the courts in Tibet having heavy tasks of maintaining stability and low existing equipment levels, and give priority to including the business technical equipment, comprehensive support equipment, and judicial police equipment needed by the courts in Tibet in the equipment allocation plan and annual implementation plan, striving to meet the standards as soon as possible, with the required expenses fully guaranteed by the central finance.

13. Actively implement the central government's guarantee policies for infrastructure construction of the courts in Tibet. In accordance with the spirit of the "Notice of the General Office of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the General Office of the State Council on Forwarding the 'Opinions on Strengthening the Guarantee Work for Political and Legal Funds'", the Supreme People's Court will, together with the National Development and Reform Commission, coordinate with relevant central departments to include the newly built or renovated infrastructure projects of the courts in Tibet into the "Twelfth Five-Year Plan" plan of the Tibet Autonomous Region, and give priority consideration in project and fund arrangements. Fully consider the characteristics of the courts in Tibet, and strive to include special facilities for maintaining stability, etc., of the courts in Tibet in the "Standards for the Construction of People's Court Courtrooms".

14. Actively support the implementation of the "Warmth Project" in the courts of Tibet. People's courts nationwide shall actively support the High People's Court of the Tibet Autonomous Region in implementing the "Warmth Project" in the grassroots people's courts and intermediate people's courts in Tibet, improve the working conditions and living environment of judges and staff, and strive to solve the problems of difficulty in retaining talent and unstable teams in the courts of Tibet. The Supreme People's Court shall strive to raise RMB 8 million from its own funds to help the High People's Court of the Tibet Autonomous Region launch the construction project of a transit station for cadres entering and leaving Tibet in Linzhi. Each court providing paired assistance to Tibet shall actively raise funds to support the construction of the "Three Small Warmth Projects" (small emergency standby duty officer dormitory, small staff activity room, small living service room) in the 73 grassroots people's courts and the "Two Small Warmth Projects" (emergency standby duty room, staff activity room) in the 7 intermediate people's courts in Tibet, striving to complete within three years. The High People's Court of the Tibet Autonomous Region shall organize each grassroots people's court, based on the principle of "one-time planning, step-by-step implementation", to refine project content, and, in accordance with the authorized staffing and prescribed standards, put forward the amount of funds to be provided by the paired courts on a practical basis, ensuring implementation as scheduled.

VI. Reasonably Set Up People's Tribunals in Tibet

15. Effectively facilitate the people's litigation. On the basis of the "three orientations" and the "two conveniences" principles, in accordance with the requirements of facilitating circuit trials, timely and reasonably adjust and scientifically lay out the setting of people's tribunals in Tibet. Equip equipment suitable for local natural conditions and circuit trial work, improve the circuit trial working mechanism, strengthen the construction of circuit trial points, and effectively solve the people's difficulty in filing lawsuits.

VII. Increase Support for the Courts in the Tibetan Areas of Sichuan, Yunnan, Gansu, and Qinghai Provinces

16. Seriously study and implement specific measures to support the courts in the Tibetan areas of the four provinces. The high people's courts of the four provinces shall, based on the actual situation of the courts in the Tibetan areas of their own provinces, in accordance with the spirit of the Fifth Central Symposium on Work in Tibet, according to their respective characteristics, adhere to the principle of combining strengthening policy support with giving full play to their own potential, improve the intra-provincial assistance mechanism, and study the establishment of a paired assistance mechanism, achieving coordinated advancement and common development. The Supreme People's Court, in accordance with the overall requirements of the Central Committee, shall cooperate with the high people's courts of the four provinces to study and formulate project plans and specific policy measures to support the development of courts in the Tibetan areas, help solve the prominent problems and difficulties they face, and implement various policy measures determined by the Central Committee.

VIII. Steadily Promote the Construction of Working Mechanisms

17. Continuously improve the working mechanism for assistance to Tibet. Establish and improve a working mechanism that is vertically and horizontally connected, with each performing its own duties, coordinated and orderly, and efficient in operation, striving to form a work pattern where the Supreme People's Court's Leading Group for Assistance to Tibet conducts overall coordination, courts providing assistance earnestly perform their duties, and recipient courts organize implementation. The Supreme People's Court is responsible for planning, guiding, and managing the assistance work for Tibet, coordinating and implementing corresponding policies and measures, and focusing on solving major problems in the assistance work for Tibet. Conduct supervision and inspection of the assistance work for Tibet, summarize experience, commend and reward excellent collectives and advanced individuals, strengthen positive publicity, and set up outstanding models.

18. Work requirements for courts providing paired assistance to Tibet. High people's courts shall uniformly coordinate and arrange the relevant work of the courts in their province (municipality) providing paired assistance to Tibet. Courts providing assistance shall establish a leadership institution for assistance work to Tibet, headed by the main leader and participated by the responsible leaders and heads of relevant departments, specifically responsible for the implementation, management, and coordination of the assistance work for Tibet. They shall regard the paired assistance work as an important task and incorporate it into the overall work plan and annual work plan. They shall earnestly find the combination points of the advantageous resources of the two places, and continuously expand the fields of paired assistance. Actively seek support from the Party Committee and government, and strive to include the assistance projects and budget funds for Tibet into the overall plan of the local government for paired assistance to Tibet.

19. Relevant responsibilities of the High People's Court of the Tibet Autonomous Region. It shall earnestly implement the requirements of the Central Committee and the Supreme People's Court for doing a good job in assistance work for Tibet, regularly organize investigations, research, supervision, and inspection of the assistance work for Tibet, actively propose assistance project suggestions to the Supreme People's Court, and promptly report the progress of assistance projects to the Supreme People's Court. It shall strengthen communication and liaison with the high people's courts of the provinces (municipalities) providing paired assistance to Tibet, overall coordinate and solve the difficulties and problems encountered by the courts providing paired assistance during the assistance process. The High People's Court of the Tibet Autonomous Region shall take this opportunity to fully strengthen the team building of the courts in the entire region, continuously improve the level of law enforcement, enhance judicial capacity, and effectively safeguard social fairness and justice.

20. Work requirements for recipient courts. Actively prepare for receiving assistance projects, proactively communicate and liaise with the paired courts providing assistance, strengthen coordination and cooperation, and earnestly organize the implementation of assistance projects. Establish and improve the management system and supervision and inspection mechanism for assistance projects and assistance funds, and strive to maximize the effectiveness of limited funds. Do a good job in receiving cadres sent to assist Tibet, care about the work and life of cadres sent to assist Tibet in Tibet, and actively create conditions for their work and study. People's courts at all levels in the Tibet Autonomous Region shall continue to carry forward the spirit of self-reliance and hard struggle, and continuously improve their work level.

Attachment: List of National People's Courts Providing Paired Assistance to the Courts in Tibet
